text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: autoscale-throttle-rate high on us-west-2 serving-pool-3 (tokens/sec spike, throttle events 230 in 5m)
alex: I’m on it, grabbing the runbook.
maria: I can be second on calls if needed, what’s the customer impact?
devon: Seeing increased 503 and 429s in the logs, looks like backpressure from queue depth + token limit. Example log: `throttle event client_id=web-frontend reason=queue_depth_exceeded tokens=512`
alex: Paging SRE oncall. Starting mitigation steps: scale up dedicated pool by +2 GPUs, increase burst capacity for 10m, enable fallback model route to smaller-quantized variant.
infra-bot: scale request accepted: pool serving-pool-3 +2 gpus (requested by alex) — ETA 90s
lucy: I’m watching customer error dashboards; top 5 customers by errors are mid-market orgs in NA. No billing spikes but retention requests failing.
maria: Can we throttle non-interactive batch traffic first? Is there request tagging to differentiate?
devon: Yes, route meta:traffic_type=batch. I just pushed a quick rule to deprioritize batch in the queue: `priority: realtime > interactive > batch`
alex: After deprioritizing batch we saw queue depth drop ~30% within 40s. Throttle events down to ~140 in the next minute. Scaling still in progress.
incident-bot: Note: incident severity elevated to P2 due to customer impact on realtime endpoints.
maria: I'll message CS to prepare customer comms if degradation persists.
devon: Quick dashboard snippet I’m watching: queries/sec, tokens/sec, queue_depth_90, throttle_rate. Suggest adding a combined metric for tokens_per_second_per_gpu to detect saturation earlier.
lucy: Agree. Current queue_depth threshold is 500, but with our new batching improvements that correlates poorly with throttle. We should tune to tokens/sec per GPU and token backlog.
alex: For immediate mitigation, we’ve completed scale +2 and manually raised autoscale target by 25% for 15m; fallback model routed 40% of traffic. Error rate dropped to baseline after 4m.
infra-bot: scale complete. pool serving-pool-3 now at desired capacity.
maria: Good. After-action: we need an alert tuning plan. I propose:
- Replace single absolute queue_depth alert with two signals: tokens/sec per GPU (warn at 70% of target) and sustained queue_growth_rate (5m).
- Add an early-warning synthetic check on representative prompt types that measure tokens/sec and latency.
- Debounce throttle_event alert to 3m with count threshold 20 to reduce noise.
devon: Also recommend creating a dashboard tile: `tokens/sec per GPU (p95)` and `queue growth rate` with anomaly shading. Will add panel to eng-sre:autoscale-overview.
lucy: Runbook edits: add batch deprioritization step, include exact CLI to bump burst capacity and the fallback model config.
alex: Action items assigned: devon add dashboard + alert rule changes (tokens/sec per GPU alert), lucy update runbook, maria coordinate postmortem and customer comms, alex follow up with infra to consider autoscale policy change (factor in tokens/sec).
maria: Timeline for follow-up PRs? dashboard + alert change PR in 48h, runbook update in 24h, postmortem draft in 72h.
devon: I'll open PR for dashboard + alert now and link here.
incident-bot: Incident resolved: error rates returned to baseline, alerts cleared. Recording incident timeline for postmortem.
alex: Thanks team — nice quick mitigation. We'll meet tomorrow 10:00 PT to finalize tuning thresholds and rollout canary for updated autoscaler policy.
maria: Noted. Adding owners to calendar invite. :thumbsup:
lucy: Quick note for the postmortem: include customer impact window (09:12–09:19 UTC), mitigation steps and metric deltas (queue depth -35%, throttle events -81% after scale+fallback).
devon: Saved logs + traces in /var/logs/incidents/2001112223/ and linked to the PR.
alex: Closing thread once follow-ups are tracked. Thanks.
